recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No FHIR-core source follow-up is needed for FHIR-31846 unless a future work-group decision changes the ClinicalUseDefinition type/backbone model.
issue_request: FHIR-31846 was a Published/Persuasive BRR FHIR-core ClinicalUseIssue request to add an invariant because one issue cannot simultaneously be a contraindication, interaction, undesirable effect, or other detailed clinical-use kind.
initial_application: No current git commit explicitly mentioning FHIR-31846 was found. The cud-1 invariant appears in source history in 13b7d768e64 during the ClinicalUseIssue to ClinicalUseDefinition rename, and later commits added warning to the kind set and corrected the contraindication expression path.
additional_context: ClinicalUseIssue is no longer the active current-build resource; source/fhir.ini comments ClinicalUseIssue and actively builds ClinicalUseDefinition. Later FHIR-48893 added cud-2 through cud-6 type/backbone matching constraints, which are compatible with retaining cud-1 as the FHIR-31846 one-kind guardrail. Corrected Zulip and Confluence searches found no conflicting community evidence.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit because source/clinicalusedefinition/structuredefinition-ClinicalUseDefinition.xml already contains cud-1 and source/clinicalusedefinition/invariant-tests/cud-1.f1.fail.xml exercises the invalid multi-kind case.

related_jiras.note: The rename from ClinicalUseIssue to ClinicalUseDefinition carried the invariant into the current resource name.

Later BRR work added matching type/backbone invariants that reinforce the single-kind model.
